title: Terminator-seq normalization to resolve customer eval regressions from fallback routing
creator: Anika Patel
description: Multiple customers reported subtle eval score regressions and trailing prompt artifacts after a sampling-defaults harmonization and a routing fallback optimization. Affected environments: Hosted (routing -> fallback model variants), Dedicated pools with fallback enabled, and Private deployments that had legacy sampling overrides.
timeline: 2026-02-18: First inbound from Customer A (finance) reporting truncated JSON fields and extra suffix lines in eval outputs
2026-02-19: Duplicate reports from Customers B and C during scheduled sanity evaluations; support elevated severity
2026-02-20: Triage call, assigned to ENG-ops on-call
2026-02-21: Hypothesis formed: sampling default harmonization changed termination precedence when routing fallback occurs

steps_to_reproduce: Create a multi-tenant request that triggers routing fallback (hosted -> dedicated variant or dedicated -> fallback-quantized)
Submit a prompt containing explicit termination tokens and nested function-call markers
Use runtime sampling defaults introduced in runtime-2.3.0 (top_p/temperature harmonization)
Replay traffic and observe trailing/doubled tokens appended after expected stop conditions
root_cause: The routing/fallback layer merged termination sequences and sampling defaults from primary and fallback model configs in a non-deterministic way. On fallback, the merged config could reorder or duplicate terminator tokens and inherit sampling parameters that changed stop-token precedence. KV-cache reuse across model variants exposed a stop-token normalization bug allowing suffix emission post-canonical stop.
mitigation: 1) Hosted emergency hotfix: enforce canonical termination sequence normalization in routing and apply stop-token precedence before sampling. 2) Backport patch to Dedicated orchestrator images and schedule rolling updates. 3) Provide a one-line config patch and guidance for Private deployments. 4) Add regression tests to eval harness and daily replay tests for fallback scenarios.
implementation_notes: Canonicalizer enforces deterministic ordering for termination markers: dedupe, normalize encoding, stable sort
Config inheritance now treats termination sequences as immutable/high-precedence values during fallback merges
Added KV-cache invalidation hook when model-variant prefix lengths differ by >16 tokens to avoid bleed-through
Trade-off: deterministic canonicalization can change edge-case termination ordering for legacy prompts; prioritized parity and predictability over preserving ambiguous legacy orders
